findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Bags of eggs, still partially frozen, were observed in a bus tub of standing water in the first compartment of the 3 part sink. Cold water was turned on and allowed to flow over product to finish thawing. Thawing was discussed, and educational handout was provided.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
760.510 - Certified food manager was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. 

Persons handling food shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food or clean equipment.
NOTE: After drying hands with paper towels, use the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet to avoid contamination of freshly washed hands. (Refer to posted handwashing technique sign at handsink for details)

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

Observed: 1) a cup pf tea on the cook line 2) a can of tea on a self in the dry storage 3) a bottle of Pepsi stored in the chest freezer. Foods should be stored in designated areas separate from foods to be cooked/ distributed for public consumption. Discussed with person in charge (PIC) and instructed to remove.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
750-810b Moist wiping cloths should be stored in sanitizing solution between uses.

Observed wiping cloths in 2 locations to be moist and stored on counters in the bar area and the cook line. Discussed with the PIC and instructed to move cloths to correct sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Uncovered cup of yellow liquid was observed in the beer cooler. Casey's manager stated it appeared to be sweet and sour. The liquid was discarded. 
Foods shall be protected at all times. Provide covers on cups and other containers used for storage of beverages and mixers. Make sure containers and cups are also labeled as to the contents.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside holder for soda gun (mold/buildup);  and
B) inside ice bin (debris).

Clean and sanitize the aforementioned items prior to the next use. Also, clean and sanitize the aforementioned items as needed, and maintain them clean to eliminate buildup of debris and prevent cross contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1050 - A metal beer bucket full of moldy waste water was observed inside the keg cooler. Waste water was discarded during the inspection by Casey's manager.
NOTE: Empty the bucket used to catch waste water from the keg cooler drain line at the end of every event.

All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.
